affordance_in_statement: A triplet of modules T is classified as unresolvable if every possible assignment of operating modes to its three modules produces at least one conflicting bus.
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal that preserves the task: on exactly three vertices, the quantified two-mode condition is intrinsically equivalent to requiring all three buses, i.e. a triangle. Only a semantic change to the configuration size or conflict rule would eliminate this reduction.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Reduces an unresolvable triplet to a triangle and finds the smallest triangle using bitset intersections.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: A triplet is unresolvable when every binary mode assignment has a same-mode bus conflict.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Enumerates ordered triplets and tests whether all three pairwise buses exist.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The definition quantifies over all mode assignments on only three modules.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses adjacency bitsets and ordered neighbors to search for triangles in lexicographic order.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: An unresolvable three-module induced graph is exactly a non-bipartite three-vertex graph, hence a triangle.

common_affordance: The unresolvable-triplet condition is intrinsically equivalent to finding a triangle in the bus graph.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The code iterates candidates in input edge order ("for u, v in edges") rather than guaranteeing lexicographic candidate order, so returning the first discovered triangle can violate the required lexicographic tie-break.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat all survivors while preserving the stated task. Any effective edit would have to change the semantics—such as using more than three modules per candidate or changing the conflict rule—because the triangle reduction is the core structure.
regression_risk: A change that merely makes candidate generation or edge order less direct could accidentally restore glm-5 if it also causes its first discovered triangle to be lexicographically smallest.
